title: Clean samples with plasma
summary: Prepare compatible samples, complete a manually sequenced plasma cleaning cycle, and recover the samples safely. Placeholder content for manual-control mode only; the owner must confirm the installed unit's mode (SOP mode: __) before use. This is general laboratory content, not the manufacturer's manual.

steps.title: Switch on the unit and pump
steps.body: Switch on the rear power switch and pump at the rear panel, and confirm the PLC display lights. Keep RF power disabled.

steps.title: Check the gas supply
steps.body: Confirm that the connected gas and supply pressure match the locally approved cleaning recipe (SOP gas: __; supply pressure: __ [units: __]). Check the visible tubing and flowmeter for damage, and keep the process gas valve closed until the pumping sequence calls for flow.
steps.caution: An incorrect gas or damaged gas line can create an unsafe discharge; stop and notify the instrument owner if either is uncertain.

steps.title: Open the chamber door
steps.body: Confirm that plasma power is off and the chamber has reached atmospheric pressure through the approved vent sequence. Release the latch and swing the door clear without forcing it.
steps.caution: A door that resists opening may still be held by vacuum; forcing the latch can damage the seal.

steps.title: Place samples on the electrode tray
steps.body: Use clean tweezers to place dry, approved samples flat on the electrode tray with space between them. Keep samples away from the chamber wall and door seal, and remove loose debris using the local cleaning method.
steps.caution: Wet samples, loose powders, or incompatible materials can contaminate the chamber or react during plasma exposure.

steps.title: Close and latch the door
steps.body: Inspect the sealing surface for debris and confirm that no sample projects into the door opening. Close the door gently and secure its latch as trained.
steps.check: Samples are clear of the seal, the door is fully latched, and hands and tools are outside the chamber.

steps.title: Set cleaning time and power
steps.body: Confirm on the PLC that this unit uses the owner-approved manual-control mode (owner-confirmed SOP mode: __). Steps 06–08 describe manual pump, gas, RF, and vent sequencing; if the unit is configured for an automatic PLC cycle, stop and use its owner-approved automatic-cycle SOP instead. Enter the recipe exposure time and power (SOP: __ s, __ W). Review both values and keep plasma power disabled while preparing the vacuum.

steps.title: Pump down and establish gas flow
steps.body: Start pump-down in manual mode and watch the pressure decrease. Once the display shows the recipe base pressure (SOP: __ [pressure units: __]), open the flowmeter valve to the recipe flow (SOP: __ sccm) and wait for pressure to stabilise in the operating band (SOP: __ to __ [pressure units: __]).
steps.caution: Failure to reach a stable operating pressure can indicate a leak or incorrect flow; do not ignite the plasma to compensate.

steps.title: Run the plasma cycle
steps.body: Enable RF for the timed plasma exposure in manual mode with the door latched and the operating pressure stable. Monitor the pressure and instrument status throughout the run, and use the trained stop sequence if there is arcing, an alarm, or unstable operation.
steps.check: The door is latched, pressure and gas flow match the recipe, and the exposure time and power have been reviewed.

steps.title: Stop gas flow and vent
steps.body: Confirm that the timed RF exposure has ended and plasma power is off, then close the process gas valve. Follow the local pump isolation and controlled vent sequence, waiting until the pressure indicates atmosphere and the samples have cooled to the handling range (SOP: __ to __ °C).

steps.title: Open the door and recover samples
steps.body: After confirming atmospheric pressure and safe handling temperature, release the latch and open the door fully. Remove samples with clean tweezers, place them in a labeled container, and continue to end of session.
